item.text:
Mixed, leaning negative. I found real 2024 evidence of AML/CFT and procurement-rule tightening, but the broader integrity environment still showed executive-controlled procurement, opaque SOEs, and politically aligned business structures.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring - June 2024 | FATF | 2024-06-28 | https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/publications/High-risk-and-other-monitored-jurisdictions/increased-monitoring-june-2024.html | FATF said Türkiye made “significant progress” and was removed from increased monitoring after strengthening AML/CFT supervision, sanctions, beneficial-ownership rules, financial intelligence use, and money-laundering/terror-financing prosecutions. This is meaningful anti-corruption-adjacent reform, but it is technical and financial-integrity focused rather than a full assault on patronage networks. | 5B.5, 5B.3 |
| Positive | Republic of Türkiye: 2024 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for the Republic of Türkiye | IMF | 2024-10-11 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/11/republic-of-trkiye-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-statement-by-556139 | IMF’s 2024 Article IV report says authorities made legal and regulatory updates to improve AML/CFT, including addressing shortcomings related to politically exposed persons, and notes a new anti-corruption strategy was being prepared. This supports some integrity-building capacity, though the IMF still called for further reforms. | 5B.5, 5B.3 |
| Positive | Public Announcement | Devlet Malzeme Ofisi Genel Müdürlüğü | 2024-03-18 | https://www.dmo.gov.tr/Eng/Home/EngIcerik/3921 | The State Supply Office said its procurement procedures must ensure transparency, competition, equal treatment, reliability, confidentiality, public scrutiny, timeliness, and efficient use of resources. This is a narrow but real rule-based procurement statement. | 5B.5, 5B.4 |
| Negative | Turkey - Transparency.org | Transparency International | 2025-03-28 | https://www.transparency.org/en/nis/countries/turkey | TI says procurement-law exceptions remain high and keep expanding, procurement data are fragmented, the Public Procurement Authority is appointed by executive discretion without open selection or parliamentary oversight, and whistleblower protection is absent. That is strong evidence against a fair, anti-favoritism procurement regime. | 5B.5, 5B.4 |
| Negative | Turkey - Transparency.org | Transparency International | 2025-03-28 | https://www.transparency.org/en/nis/countries/turkey?status=notImplemented&view=recommendations | TI says most SOEs do not have to disclose financial information, the Türkiye Wealth Fund is exempt from Court of Accounts audits, and SOE boards are filled through opaque presidential appointments with politically aligned individuals. This is direct evidence of politically controlled business privilege and weak oversight. | 5B.5, 5B.4 |
| Negative | Turkey | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey | Reuters Institute said government-friendly brands such as CNN Türk and A Haber, plus the public broadcaster TRT, gave disproportionate airtime to incumbents. That is indirect but useful evidence of a politically connected conglomerate/media ecosystem rather than a neutral competitive market. | 5B.5, 4B.6 |

Search gap: I did not find strong 2024 primary-source evidence that Erdoğan personally dismantled oligarchic capture, prosecuted politically connected business elites, or made procurement authorities genuinely independent. The best positives are AML/CFT compliance and formal procurement language; the structural evidence on SOEs, procurement, and executive appointments still points the other way.
